page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.2xlarge is a storage-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8559C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 8 vCPUs across 4 dedicated physical cores with hyperthreading. The processor includes 320 MB of L3 cache alongside specialized instruction extensions including AVX-512, Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for INT8 and BF16 formats, and hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions. The server includes 64.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation.

Local physical storage is a central component of the i7ie.2xlarge architecture, featuring a bundled 5,000 GB NVMe SSD that delivers direct, high-capacity, low-latency disk storage without requiring external network-attached volumes. For network input and output, the instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs included on this server configuration.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded compute and memory capabilities, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2,312.0 in the top 10% tier and a top-tier text processing rating of 2,963.0. Single-threaded compression throughput is similarly competitive, reaching 34.73 GB/sec in gzip and 14.03 GB/sec in bzip3. Memory subsystem benchmarks show high cached small-block read speeds of 681.16 GB/sec and uncached memory bandwidth of 63.39 GB/sec read and 58.36 GB/sec write. Multi-core performance aligns with its 4-core, 8-vCPU footprint, recording 8,788.32 on stress-ng multi-core and 15,605.17 on PassMark CPU tests. Redis SET operations measured 12.25 million operations per second.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of 5,000 GB of local NVMe storage with 64.0 GB of memory offers a dense storage-to-compute ratio. The primary tradeoff lies in raw parallel processing capability; larger scale compute jobs or medium-to-large language model inference tasks show constrained throughput due to core counts, recording 6.9 tokens per second for text generation on a 7B parameter model. Consequently, the i7ie.2xlarge is best positioned for I/O-intensive databases, distributed file systems, caching clusters, and transactional search workloads requiring local non-volatile storage.
description: Amazon Web Services i7ie.2xlarge is a storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System, equipped with an 8-vCPU Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.2 GHz across 4 physical cores. It features 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 6 GHz and a dedicated 5,000 GB NVMe SSD for high-capacity local storage, paired with an 8 Gbps baseline network link. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier single-core performance with a Geekbench single-core score of 2,312.0, robust single-threaded compression throughput, and high memory bandwidth, while multi-threaded tasks align predictably with its 4-core physical design. The instance contains no GPUs, and larger language model inference shows hardware limitations. The dense local storage and balanced memory configuration make the i7ie.2xlarge well aligned for storage-bound applications, including relational databases, NoSQL datastores, distributed storage engines, and search indexing nodes requiring low-latency NVMe access.
